questions.prompt: Which change affects **what Claude may do without asking**?
questions.explanation: Permission modes control approval. Model, effort and fast mode change which Claude runs and how it thinks or how fast it answers — not what it may do.

questions.prompt: A blog post recommends `claude --permission-mode yolo`. What happens?
options: The CLI rejects the value: yolo isn't a mode
questions.explanation: The CLI accepts acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk and plan. "YOLO" is community slang for skipping permissions.

questions.prompt: In `bypassPermissions` mode, a project deny rule `Bash(curl *)` exists. Claude runs `curl https://example.com`. Result?
options: It is denied: deny rules block in every mode
questions.explanation: Deny rules block in every mode, including bypassPermissions. Allow rules have no effect in bypass; explicit ask rules still prompt.

cards.back: Reads run; edits and non-read-only commands prompt. The safe default.
Auto-accepts file edits and common filesystem commands (mkdir, touch, mv, cp) in the working directory; other commands still prompt.
Read-only exploration and a plan; source edits wait until you approve the plan.
A background classifier reviews commands and protected-path writes instead of prompting you; working-directory edits run.
Anything that would prompt is denied; reads, read-only commands and pre-approved tools still run. For locked-down CI.
Skips permission prompts (deny rules and explicit ask rules still apply). Isolated containers or VMs only.
deny > ask > allow.
.git, .claude, .vscode, .mvn and similar: writes are never auto-approved except in bypassPermissions.
Project settings can't set defaultMode to auto or bypassPermissions.

interactions.title: Check: hook exit codes and limits

questions.prompt: A PreToolUse hook prints a message to stderr and exits 1. What happens to the tool call?
options: It proceeds — only exit 2 (or a JSON deny) blocks
questions.explanation: Exit 2 blocks and sends stderr to Claude. Other non-zero codes are non-blocking errors.

questions.prompt: A PostToolUse hook exits 2 because a Java file contains tabs. What happens?
options: The edit stays; Claude sees stderr and can fix the file next
questions.explanation: PostToolUse runs after the tool succeeded. Exit 2 is feedback, not an undo.

questions.prompt: A guard hook uses jq, which isn't installed. Which behaviour is safest?
options: Exit 2 with a message: fail closed
questions.explanation: Without jq the guard can't inspect input; failing closed blocks until the dependency is fixed instead of silently allowing everything.

cards.back: Runs before a tool call; can block (exit 2) or return allow / deny / ask.
Runs after a tool succeeds; exit 2 shows stderr to Claude as feedback.
Runs at start, resume and after compaction; stdout is added to Claude's context.
Runs when Claude finishes; decision "block" or exit 2 keeps it working. Check stop_hook_active.
Runs when Claude needs your attention (permission_prompt, idle_prompt). Personal settings.
JSON on stdin: session_id, cwd, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input …
Blocks where the event allows it; stderr goes to Claude.

options: stdout carries protocol messages, so the log line corrupts the stream
questions.explanation: In stdio transport, stdout is the protocol channel. Log to stderr.

questions.explanation: A run that failed before doing anything (e.g. not logged in) can still report subtype success. Scripts must check the exit code and is_error.

questions.prompt: What does `--bare` change for a CI run?

questions.prompt: When does the Claude Code GitHub Action run in automation mode?

questions.explanation: With a prompt it runs on the workflow event; without one it waits for the trigger phrase (interactive mode).

questions.prompt: On the orderdesk starter, POST without a discount code returns 500 but the order is stored. Why?
options: create() isn't transactional: save commits, then building the response throws
questions.explanation: Without @Transactional the repository save commits on its own. With it, the unchecked exception rolls the save back (verified: 1 row vs 0).

questions.prompt: The app fails at startup with `Schema validation: missing column [paid_at] in table [orders]`. Best fix?
questions.explanation: Fix forward with a new migration; never edit an applied one; keep validation on.
